newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian jurist seeks to revive CVRD injunction.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian jurist seeks to revive CVRD injunction.

text.p: A Brazilian jurist who succeeded in holding up the privatization of mining giant Cia. Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) for a week has appealed to a high court which overturned his injunction Monday, a court spokeswoman said.
Celso Antonio Bandeira de Mello faxed an appeal to the president of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) Tuesday and a decision was expected later today, the spokeswoman said.
If upheld, the appeal would be yet another obstacle in the way of the government's plan to privatize CVRD. The STJ is Brazil's highest court for non-constitutional matters.

The auction of 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares actually began earlier today, but was suspended when a court official walked into the Rio stock exchange waving a fresh injunction issued by a Rio court.

The STJ spokeswoman said she believed Bandeira de Mello, a private attorney, was arguing that Monday's decision by a STJ judge to overrule a series of injunctions against the CVRD sale, including his own, conflicted with an earlier ruling in favor of his injunction.

Last week, STJ president Romildo Bueno de Souza rejected a government appeal against Bandeira de Mello's injunction, arguing that any challenge had to be first heard in a regional tribunal in Sao Paulo where the injunction was issued.
